title: Generative modelling powered by room-temperature polariton condensates
authors: Yuan Wang, Marcin Muszynski, Avinash Dash, Rishabh Kaurav, Vinod M. Menon, Oleksandr Kyriienko
abstract: Generative modelling requires efficient stochastic nonlinear transformations and physical platforms that can naturally realise them. We experimentally demonstrate that nonlinear optical systems operating in the strong light-matter coupling regime can serve as physical transformation layers for conditional generative modelling. Specifically, we develop a workflow in which room-temperature exciton-polariton condensates formed in organic dye microcavities act as a physical stochastic transform within a generative adversarial network and enable conditional digit-to-image translation. By using the nonlinear many-body dynamics and intrinsic stochasticity of polariton condensates, the workflow outperforms baseline approaches based on digitally injected perturbations. We find that polariton-enabled sampling via generative adversarial network (Polariton GAN) yields improved inception score, digit preservation accuracy and structural similarity compared with both digital sampling and laser-based systems. We further show that spatially correlated output variations can naturally regularise adversarial training and enhance output diversity. Our results establish polariton condensation as a new computational resource for generative modelling, opening a pathway towards physics-enhanced machine learning systems.
summary: The paper demonstrates that nonlinear optical systems, specifically room-temperature exciton-polariton condensates, can function as physical stochastic layers within Generative Adversarial Networks. By using the inherent dynamics of these condensates for data sampling in digit-to-image translation, they achieve superior performance compared to purely digital noise injection methods. This establishes polariton condensation as a novel computational resource for physics-enhanced machine learning.
main_problem: The core challenge is developing generative models that require efficient stochastic nonlinear transformations, necessitating the use of physical platforms to overcome computational limitations.
main_result: Polariton condensation was successfully demonstrated as a viable room-temperature photonic resource for conditional generative modeling, outperforming purely digital or laser-based sampling methods in terms of image quality and diversity.
method: A workflow integrating a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) with the nonlinear dynamics of exciton-polariton condensates is employed to perform conditional digit-to-image translation.
model_or_system: The physical system utilizes room-temperature exciton-polariton condensates formed in organic dye microcavities, which provide a naturally stochastic and nonlinear transformation layer for the GAN's latent space.
key_observables: Inception Score (IS), Digit Preservation Accuracy (DPA), Structural Similarity Index (SSIM), and Pixel Variance are used to quantify generation quality, diversity, and semantic correctness.
important_parameters: Strong light-matter coupling regime; operating temperature near room temperature; the nonlinear many-body dynamics of polaritons.
main_assumptions: The intrinsic stochasticity and spatially correlated nature of the polariton condensate's nonlinear response can be harnessed as a structured computational resource for generative modeling.
figures_summary: Figures compare performance metrics (IS, DPA) across condensate-enabled GANs versus digital baseline methods, showing superior results for the former. Other figures illustrate PL spectra and the workflow setup.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the need for physical stochastic transformations in generative modeling; it details the experimental realization using polariton condensates as a physical layer within a conditional GAN framework; finally, it presents quantitative comparisons proving the superiority of this physics-enhanced approach over digital baselines.
why_interesting: This work directly bridges condensed matter/quantum optics (polaritons) with machine learning (GANs), proposing a concrete pathway for realizing physics-based hardware accelerators for AI tasks, which is highly relevant to open quantum systems research.

The resulting photoluminescence (PL) produces transformed digit images through nonlinear condensate dynamics.
